transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-20 15:30 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Austin (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SA), Maya (Silverline Head Security), Rohit (Eng Manager), Jenna (Compliance), Alex (DevOps)

Summary: quick SOC two / ISO two seven oh one posture review, go over reports, trust center access, mapping to their controls, and the deets on RBAC SSO KMS and residency.

00:00 Austin: All right hi everyone thanks for joining, um this is Austin from Redwood, i'll hand it to Priya to run the posture review, i'm here for commercial questions and follow ups
00:12 Priya: Hey thanks Austin, hi Maya, Rohit, Jenna, Alex — uh quick agenda, we'll run through our SOC 2 type two artifacts and ISO 27001 coverage, talk trust center access, show where audit logs live, then deep dive on encryption/KMS and deployment options. Feel free to interrupt.
00:30 Maya: Sounds good, our main ask — we are about to start a pilot with patient data, PHI, and need to ensure we have mapped controls for our internal auditors and third party. We also want to see evidence or how to get auditor access.
00:45 Priya: Yep totally. Quick background: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering our hosted platform, and our ISO 27001 scope covers the inference control plane and management layer; for private/onsite we provide a different evidence set. We have a Trust Center link that lists the certs and you can request read-only auditor access — i'll share that after the call.
01:12 Rohit: When you say "hosted platform" does that include model hosting and logs? we need to know where audit logs live, retention, and exportability.
01:25 Priya: Good Q. For hosted, we capture request/response metadata (not full sensitive payload by default), auth events, admin actions, and deployment events. Logs are available via the console and we can export them via S3 or syslog streams for long-term retention. Retention defaults to 90 days but we have add-on options.
01:44 Jenna: Are the logs filtered for PHI? we can't have PHI stored in logs per our policy.
01:52 Priya: Right — by default we redact payloads and policy prevents logging full prompt/response bodies for customers with PHI. There's a flag during onboarding — we can enable strict no-payload-logging mode; in dedicated/private you control the storage. I'll note that and share the exact setting.
02:18 Alex: For private deployment, do you support an on-prem package or is it VPC-only in cloud? Our infra team prefers VPC peering and customer-managed networking.
02:29 Liam: We support both. Redwood Private can be deployed into your VPC with a customer-managed control plane; for air-gapped on-prem we provide an on-prem bundle and we can arrange HSM/KMS integrations. For VPC we do peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud.
02:48 Maya: KMS — we need to use our own KMS keys and HSM. how does Redwood handle keys at rest for models and logs?
02:57 Priya: You can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via your cloud KMS; we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. For on-prem/HSM we support integration through our key management connectors and can attest to crypto controls. All data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed keys when configured.
03:20 Rohit: What's the default encryption in hosted if we don't enable BYOK?
03:26 Priya: Default is provider-managed encryption with AES-256 at rest; keys are managed by Redwood's cloud tenancy. If you need customer-managed keys for compliance, enable BYOK.
03:34 Jenna: For ISO 27001, can you show coverage mapping to our controls? we have to map clause A.8 around asset management and A.9 for access control.
03:46 Priya: Absolutely — we maintain a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps our policies and technical controls to SOC 2 and ISO clauses. i'll attach that. It includes evidence references (e.g., policy docs, configuration screenshots, test reports).
04:05 Maya: Can auditors be given direct access to the Trust Center? or do you only share reports?
04:12 Austin: We typically provide the SOC 2 Type II PDF and invite auditors to the Trust Center for read-only access under an NDA; auditors can request evidence via a support workflow. For private installations we provide additional artifacts.
04:28 Maya: ok what about RBAC and SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning; we need fine grained roles for developer, infra, and security.
04:38 Priya: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. The console has RBAC roles and you can define custom roles; there's an org admin, security admin, developer role etc. We also expose role IDs via the API. We'll share sample YAML for RBAC mapping.
04:59 Rohit: any time-based access or just roles? we want temporary elevated access for debugging.
05:07 Liam: We support temporary elevated roles via our session management and you can require MFA for privilege elevation. We integrate with IdP session duration policies too.
05:20 Alex: Audit log integrity — is there tamper-evidence? we need immutable logs for some controls.
05:28 Priya: We can stream logs to your S3 with object lock enabled (WORM) or to a SIEM. We also provide signed log digests on request for attestation.
05:46 Jenna: Evidence for SOC two — how fresh are the reports? which period do they cover?
05:52 Austin: Our latest SOC 2 Type II covers the period Jan 1 2026 through Oct 31 2026; we run annual audits. The Type II includes control tests and results.
06:06 Maya: Do you have ISO 27001 certificate? is the scope limited?
06:12 Priya: We have ISO 27001 certification; scope is our inference platform and control plane, excluding customer-managed private installs. The certificate and scope statement are in the Trust Center.
06:28 Rohit: For the pilot, we're likely to start hosted but with strict no-payload-logging and BYOK; what are the latencies and performance guarantees under those settings?
06:38 Liam: BYOK adds negligible latency; encryption at rest is asynchronous for storage. Latency SLOs are more affected by model selection and whether you use Dedicated/reserved capacity. For pilot volumes we recommend starting on hosted with a reserved concurrency to keep latency predictable.
06:54 Maya: If we have a security incident, what's the notification SLA?
07:00 Priya: Incident notifications follow our security incident response; high severity incidents notify customers within one hour by email and our support portal. For Dedicated/Enterprise customers you can opt into phone paging and extended SLAs.
07:18 Jenna: Can you provide sample runbooks or evidence of IR drills?
07:23 Priya: Yes we have incident response playbooks and tabletop exercise summaries; these are annotated in the Trust Center as evidence.
07:34 Rohit: On the controls mapping — can you map your encryption controls to our internal control IDs?
07:41 Priya: We'll add a column in the spreadsheet mapping Redwood controls to Silverline control IDs. That's part of the deliverable Priya will send.
07:54 Alex: For audit logs, what fields are included? we need timestamps, actor, action, resource, request id, ip, and ideally a hash.
08:05 Priya: Those fields are present; request id and admin action markers included. IP may be redacted if required. Hashing for tamper evidence can be enabled as I mentioned.
08:20 Maya: Any issues with data residency? we need to keep data in the EU for certain customers.
08:27 Liam: Redwood can restrict data residency per-tenant; hosted supports region pinning (EU, US, APAC). For the EU you can choose an EU-only tenancy, and logs and keys can be kept in EU region. For Private installs you control physical location.
08:46 Rohit: Do you support cross-region replication for disaster recovery but still meet residency?
08:52 Priya: Cross-region replication is opt-in; if you require strict residency we disable replication outside the region. Otherwise we can replicate with encryption and key separation.
09:08 Jenna: Regarding privacy and PHI, do you sign a BAA?
09:14 Austin: Yes, we have a BAA for customers processing PHI. We'll include the BAA template and note any obligations.
09:22 Maya: ok excellent. A few additional items: our auditors will ask for evidence of role reviews and user provisioning logs over the last 12 months. Can you provide that?
09:35 Priya: We can provide provisioning audit logs and role assignment histories as part of the evidence bundle. For hosted customers we can extract a CSV; for private you control the data store.
09:49 Rohit: How do you handle model telemetry? is model training data or prompts stored? we don't want retention of user prompts.
09:58 Priya: Redwood does not store prompts for customers unless explicitly enabled for debugging/quality. For PHI customers we default to no-prompt retention and redact payloads. We keep telemetry metrics (latency, token counts) without payloads.
10:18 Maya: Regarding the Trust Center, what's the process for auditors requesting evidence?
10:24 Austin: Auditors request access via a form; we provision read-only Trust Center access under NDA and they can request evidence through the portal — we track requests and have an SLA for responses.
10:37 Jenna: Can we get a sample of the SOC 2 report redacted? like an executive summary?
10:43 Austin: I'll send the SOC 2 Type II PDF which contains the full auditor report; if you need a redacted executive summary we can produce one.
10:55 Rohit: Are there any third party subservice organizations we should be aware of? cloud providers, logging vendors?
11:03 Priya: We use major cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) depending on region and trusted logging/monitoring stacks; these are listed in our SOC 2 subservice organization appendix.
11:18 Maya: For encryption key rotation policies, do you rotate keys automatically?
11:24 Priya: If you use provider-managed keys we rotate per provider defaults; with BYOK you control rotation schedule, though we recommend annual rotation and can help automate.
11:38 Jenna: Any prior auditor findings we should know about?
11:42 Austin: No open findings in the last audit, previous findings were operational and closed. We'll include the auditor's management letter notes if relevant.
11:55 Maya: Ok sounds good, let's recap next steps.
12:00 Austin: Recap — Austin will send SOC 2 Type II report and Trust Center link; Priya will send controls mapping and RBAC examples; Alex will provide KMS policy and preferred region; Jenna will confirm auditor requirements and evidence list. We'll schedule a 30m follow-up with DevOps next week.
12:18 Rohit: timeline wise we'd like the evidence within a week to kick off the pilot the following week.
12:25 Austin: Understood we'll prioritize. Thanks everyone.
12:30 Meeting end.
